title: Neon Threat Matrix — Red Team Interface
description: A cybersecurity briefing layout built around a dark grid ground, left-rail monospace glyph sidebar, and glowing threat-level chip — optimized for internal red-team reports that demand operational credibility over visual decoration.
philosophy: This template treats the slide as a live terminal window, not a presentation canvas. It values data density and signal fidelity above all else, drawing directly from security operations center dashboards and Palantir-style dark UIs. It flatly refuses warm tones, decorative illustration, or any visual cue that might soften the severity of the content being reported. It exists for one room: analysts briefing analysts, where the audience reads IP addresses before headlines.
goodFor: Internal red-team debrief and post-incident briefings
Tabular IP address and risk-score data presentations
SOC and infosec team operational status reviews
Cybersecurity conference lightning talks on active threat intelligence
avoidFor: Executive all-hands with non-technical or mixed audiences
Brand, marketing, or product launch presentations
Proposals or pitches requiring a warm, approachable tone
Content relying on photography, illustration, or hero imagery
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a cold terminal authentication screen seconds before a classified briefing begins — dark, gridded, operationally severe. A glowing threat-level chip anchors the left rail as the sole luminous focal point in an otherwise ice-cold interface, pulling the eye before the title is even read. Composition is asymmetric and deliberately tense: a dense scrolling glyph column on the left, wide negative space on the right where the deck title surfaces with blunt authority. Avoid softness, rounded decorative forms, or any visual warmth that would undercut the operational severity this cover must signal.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a fixed left rail spanning cols 1–2, housing a vertical stack of scrolling terminal glyphs and a threat-level chip locked to the upper third of that rail. Deck title occupies cols 3–10, vertically anchored just above center-line, with the subtitle sitting directly below separated by a full-width hairline rule. A bottom strip runs edge-to-edge carrying the slide identifier, classification tag, and date stamp flush-right; outer margin holds at roughly 7% with no decorative elements allowed to bleed into the title field. Hierarchy is enforced through size contrast and the rule line alone — no banding, no background fills behind text.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a frozen SOC dashboard — cold, clinical, data-dense, every element justified by signal value. Asymmetric tension between the narrow glyph-rail and the information-packed main field implies active threat monitoring, not passive display. Neon accent glows on the threat chip and inline status indicators should read as terminal warnings, never decoration. Avoid visual softness: no rounded containers, no illustrative icons, no whitespace that reads as comfort.
